utility.notes: Seattle City Light is a municipally-owned utility serving the City of Seattle directly.

value.name: Seattle City Light (SCL)
value.notes: SCL is itself the municipal generation and distribution utility for Seattle; no separate generation supplier or CCA applies.

permit_authority.value: Seattle Department of Construction and Inspections (SDCI); electrical permits jointly coordinated with Seattle City Light
permit_authority.notes: Washington's building/electrical codes (Title 51 WAC, based on ICC model codes) apply statewide, but electrical permit issuance is split: the state Department of Labor & Industries (L&I) issues electrical permits in most jurisdictions, while Seattle (like Tacoma and a handful of other cities) administers its own electrical permits through SDCI rather than through L&I — a genuine structural distinction from most other Washington cities.

interconnection_url.notes: Per SDCI Tip #420 (jointly developed with SCL, updated 2025-07-14): customer-owned, grid-connected systems of 100kW or less qualify for SCL's Net Metering program (subject to inspection); some arrays up to 250kW qualify under a separate 'Large Solar Program.' An Interconnection Application and Agreement is required, conditional on final approval of the electrical permit. With net metering, excess electricity generated during a billing period is credited back to the customer (true retail-rate net metering, described as spinning the meter backwards).

battery_programs.notes: Per SDCI Tip #420: the electrical permit application includes an 'Energy Storage System?' checkbox triggering a 3-page ESS questionnaire; home battery systems do not require Seattle Fire Department review unless they exceed 40kWh capacity (individual home batteries typically run 9-14kWh). This describes a permitting/safety review threshold, not a financial battery incentive program, which was not independently confirmed this session.

value.name: Electrical permit — for systems up to 12kW, an Over-The-Counter (OTC) permit requiring a one-line electrical diagram and catalogue cuts
value.required_when: always, for all solar electric systems

value.name: Electrical permit plan review submission (fuller review, not the OTC path)
Building permit
value.required_when: when the rooftop solar installation does NOT meet ALL of 9 specific exemption criteria (single-family rooftop, engineered mounting system, lightweight roof material, panels ≤18in above roof surface and not exceeding the ridge height, ≤5 lb/sq ft dead load, load spread across framing sections not exceeding 50 lb per section, attachment per manufacturer spec, proper weatherproofing, and compliance with land use/fire code) — OR for ground-mounted systems, commercial/industrial systems, or building alterations valued over $6,000

value.name: Interconnection Application and Agreement with Seattle City Light
Plumbing permit (issued by Seattle/King County Public Health)

required_documents.notes: Per SDCI Tip #420, jointly developed by SDCI and Seattle City Light (updated 2025-07-14). Documents must be submitted in 11x17 format or larger, with an approved permit set kept at the project site at the same size.

value: An electrical inspection is required after installation for all solar electric systems
Systems qualifying for SCL's Net Metering program are subject to inspection

Detailed Seattle Fire Code roof-access-pathway rules apply unless the structure has automatic fire sprinklers, a roof slope ≤2:12, a solar array ≤33% of roof area and ≤1,000 sq ft with an 18in pathway maintained, or is a detached non-habitable structure

timeline_days.notes: No specific review-to-issuance day count was stated in SDCI Tip #420; the document does distinguish an Over-The-Counter (same-visit) electrical permit process for systems ≤12kW from a fuller plan-review process for systems >12kW, but does not attach specific day counts to either.

value.program_or_pathway: Building-permit-exempt path for rooftop single-family systems meeting 9 specific criteria; Over-The-Counter electrical permit for systems ≤12kW
other_conditions: SCL's standard Net Metering program covers systems up to 100kW; some arrays up to 250kW qualify under a separate Large Solar Program
Rapid Shutdown-compliant systems (per Seattle Electrical Code Section 690.12) may have certain Fire Code marking/DC-conductor-location requirements waived
RCW 36.70A.813 (statewide) requires cities/counties to allow buildings to exceed roof height limits by at least 48 inches to accommodate solar panels

value.name: Electrical permit fee, systems up to 12kW
value.unit: 1.5x the published 'base fee' (SBCC Chapter 22.900B) plus the 'administrative fee' (Chapter 22.900D, Table D-15)
value.notes: Per SDCI Tip #420. Exact dollar figures are published annually in the Permit Fee Subtitle on the Seattle Building Code Council (SBCC) website and were not independently pulled into a flat dollar amount this session.

value.name: Electrical permit fee, systems over 12kW
value.unit: 3x the published 'base fee' (SBCC Chapter 22.900B) plus the 'administrative fee' (Chapter 22.900D, Table D-15)

permit_fees.notes: The fee FORMULA is exactly and directly confirmed from the City's own document, but the underlying base-fee dollar amount (published separately and updated annually) was not independently pulled into a flat number this session.

rebates.notes: SDCI Tip #420 confirms two statewide (not Seattle-specific) financial incentives: the federal 30% investment tax credit (IRS Form 5695 for individuals) and a Washington State partial sales tax exemption/reduction for solar electric systems (dependent on system size and installation year) — no specific Seattle-only rebate dollar amount was found, so this field is left null rather than conflating the statewide incentives with a locality-specific rebate.
